target_customer: Cash-paying patients, employers, health systems and pharmacies buying generic drugs at a transparent cost plus markup
problem: Generic drug prices are inflated by wholesalers and pharmacy benefit managers. The company set out to buy generics from manufacturers and sell them at manufacturer cost plus a fixed margin.
business_model: Pharmacy and wholesale model: manufacturer cost plus a fixed 15 percent markup plus pharmacy fees
product_category: Online pharmacy and generic drug supply

founders.name: Alexander Oshmyansky
previous_startups: Osh's Affordable Pharmaceuticals (the same company under an earlier name, per YC page slug and Wikipedia)
founders.background_notes: Radiologist by training per Wikipedia and press snippets. Education and employers were not read in a source opened for this record, so they are left empty. Mark Cuban is described by Wikipedia as co-founder after a 2018 cold email pitch from Oshmyansky.

technical_complexity.rationale: A drug sourcing and fulfillment business more than a technology one. The hard parts in 2018 to 2022 were pharmacy licensing, manufacturer relationships and logistics, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Pricing transparency is copyable, but supplier relationships, state pharmacy licenses and the Mark Cuban name were hard for a new entrant to match.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied the cost plus model in a way that stopped the company. Wikipedia reports it launched in January 2022 and grew a wholesale marketplace and health system partnerships by 2024.

market_need_then: Public anger over generic drug price spikes (the 2015 Shkreli episode is cited in NBC coverage as a catalyst) and PBM opacity created demand for transparent pricing.

branding.name_origin: Delaware records reportedly show the company was renamed Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company in 2020. The name states the pricing model (cost plus margin) and borrows Cuban's personal brand. A D Magazine piece, seen only as a search snippet, says Cuban attached his name to build trust.
branding.domain_note: costplusdrugs.com, an exact descriptive domain. Acquisition details not found.

identity.logo: Not described in any opened source
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, price-transparent, consumer advocacy tone associated with Cuban's public statements

branding.brand_signature: The Mark Cuban name and the open cost plus pricing formula

rebrands.to: Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company
rebrands.why: Cuban offered to put his name on the company; source is a search snippet of D Magazine and healthimaging, not opened

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage says growth came by word of mouth with no paid marketing (Pharm Exec snippet). Snopes ran a fact check on the launch, which indicates public attention.

brand_strength.rationale: Celebrity founder backing and a self-explaining name produced heavy press and word of mouth, but the evidence is from search snippets, so the rating is moderate.

pivots.from: Selling generic drugs to pharmacies as Osh's Affordable Pharmaceuticals
pivots.to: Consumer facing online pharmacy under the Mark Cuban name, launched January 2022
pivots.why: Cuban took a larger role and renamed the company; timing per Wikipedia and press snippets

outcome_analysis: The company is active. It began as a 2018 YC generic drug wholesaler, gained Mark Cuban as investor and namesake, and launched its online pharmacy in January 2022. Brand pull from the Cuban name and anger about drug pricing drove awareness without paid marketing, and by 2024 it had added a wholesale marketplace and health system partners. Funding is not reliably public.
notes: Costplusdrugs.com about page returned 403 and the D Magazine article returned 403. Funding figures exist only on aggregators and conflict: CB Insights shows about $120K across 5 rounds, Caplight shows $1.45M with a seed in January 2019, and CB Insights lists Maveron and Asymmetry Ventures. These are unverified and not recorded as rounds. The company is a PBC and Wikipedia gives 2022 as founding year while YC lists S18. No competitor sources dated near 2018 were found; search returned only later SEO comparison pages, so the list is empty and Blink Health and GoodRx are mentioned here only as likely adjacent players. The recorded seed (2019-01-25, amount not given) rests on a single database (Caplight, which states 1.45M total funding raised). CB Insights states about 120K total. Press (D Magazine, Built In) reports Oshmyansky raised about 1M for an earlier entity before Cuban invested; no press total for the company. Total conflicts, so none summed.
